title: Productize deterministic reusable Surface worlds and secondary-world archetypes

scope.subject: Deterministic Surface world profiles, spatial content layout, primary/filler world reuse, and scalable fallback rendering inside the existing Personal Universe world stack

research_summary: Productize Surface as a reusable destination without introducing a second world application: keep ProceduralPlanets as the primary same-world terrain/atmosphere runtime, keep ProceduralTerrains Infinite World as the bounded low/software fallback, keep Astro Content Collections and the existing destination/content model as the content source, and add only a narrow deterministic world-profile/layout adapter driven by each planet's stable seed. The adapter will derive biome/atmosphere/lighting/fallback styling plus landmarks, regions, paths and clustered content anchors so secondary worlds require no hand authoring while the hero world can add richer overrides.

sources.finding: ProceduralPlanets exposes camera-inside-atmosphere rendering plus surface point/radius queries, so product landmarks and content anchors can remain attached to the same live globe instead of requiring another terrain engine.

The exploration design keeps one Planet/PlanetRenderer from astronomical approach into near-surface viewing, matching the product requirement for clean 4-to-5 landing and reverse departure continuity.

ProceduralTerrains Infinite World provides camera-centred terrain streaming with explicit chunk, triangle and frame-time budgets, making it suitable for retained low/software fallback without a finite board edge.

Astro Content Collections already provide the typed content source and loaders, so Surface spatialization should adapt the existing destination/content model rather than introduce a second CMS or Surface-specific content store.

search_ladder.conclusion: The adopted ProceduralPlanets world renderer already spans atmosphere and near-surface terrain, so the Surface product layer should extend that same world rather than replace it with a separate full solution.
The existing React Three Fiber Canvas remains the single renderer/camera lifecycle host for live planets, fallback terrain and product content anchors.

Reuse ProceduralPlanets for the primary globe, ProceduralTerrains Infinite World for fallback coverage, and Astro Content Collections for content; only deterministic profile and placement glue is missing.
Keep the existing camera-controls authority for limited Surface exploration and reverse departure rather than adding another pointer or touch navigation component.

candidates.name: Existing ProceduralPlanets same-world Surface runtime
candidates.source: Installed ProceduralPlanets 0.5.1 with existing PlanetScene/PlanetPass integration
candidates.reason: It already owns spherical terrain LOD, atmosphere, near-surface precision and surface queries, so it provides the highest-value primary renderer and preserves landing/reverse continuity.

candidates.name: Existing ProceduralTerrains Infinite World fallback with per-world profile
candidates.source: Installed procedural-terrains/infinite runtime already hosted by SurfaceTerrain
candidates.reason: It is already the approved fallback path and can consume deterministic seed/style inputs, but it remains a fallback rather than the primary globe renderer.

candidates.name: Existing Astro content and destination model spatialized onto Surface
candidates.source: Current UniverseContentEntry and destination placement pipeline
candidates.reason: Keeps authored and filler worlds on one typed content model while a deterministic adapter derives districts, paths, landmarks and clustered anchors from stable planet identity.

candidates.name: Build a separate Surface app, terrain renderer and Surface-only content store
candidates.reason: Would duplicate terrain, renderer, navigation and content authorities, break reverse travel continuity, and make secondary-world automation harder to keep reproducible.

coverage_matrix.capability: One continuous planet from atmosphere through stable Surface and reverse departure
coverage_matrix.decision: Keep ProceduralPlanets mounted as the normal Surface renderer and use the Infinite fallback only when the live globe is intentionally unavailable.

coverage_matrix.capability: Deterministic secondary worlds with stable biome, atmosphere, lighting, density and fallback appearance
coverage_matrix.decision: Add a small seed-driven profile adapter over the adopted renderers and content model instead of a second world runtime.

coverage_matrix.capability: Reusable landmarks, regions, paths and clustered content without a game-only UI
coverage_matrix.decision: Spatialize the existing content model into deterministic anchors and lightweight world-local structures while keeping content understandable as normal destinations.

coverage_matrix.capability: Readable low/software rendering with bounded work and no finite board edge
coverage_matrix.decision: Retain the approved camera-centred ProceduralTerrains Infinite fallback and feed it the same deterministic world profile with stricter budgets.

decision.rationale: Reuse the existing live planet, infinite fallback and typed content/destination layers as the product foundation. Implement only the missing deterministic world-profile and spatial-layout adapter so every planet can regenerate the same terrain/biome/lighting/content composition from stable identity, while hero worlds can layer curated overrides without creating another renderer or CMS.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: A separate app could maximize local visual freedom, but loses globally by duplicating renderer, camera, terrain and content ownership and by turning Surface into a dead-end scene switch.

decision.fallback: If a world cannot use the live ProceduralPlanets path on the selected hardware tier, render the same deterministic profile through the existing ProceduralTerrains Infinite fallback; do not add a third terrain renderer.
